name: Terovania Game Marketing Widgets for Steam®
author: Terovania Group

sections.description:
Turn website visitors into Steam wishlists and measure which placement works.

Your game’s website is where your most interested players land. This plugin puts a Steam store card with a wishlist button on any page, kept up to date from Steam, so visitors can wishlist your game right away. Your analytics shows which widget they clicked.

The widget is rendered on your server and, by default, served from your own site: no Steam iframe, no third-party scripts, no cookies set by the plugin, and no Steam API key needed.

Built for indie developers, publishers, and agencies who market games on their own websites. Install it, find your game by name in the block editor, and publish.

Three blocks for your game page

  • Steam® Game Widget: the game card with header image, description, feature icons, price, release status, platforms, and an “Add to Steam Wishlist” button. Choose the Default, Compact, or Vertical layout.
  • Steam® Screenshot Gallery: up to 20 screenshots as a grid or a scrolling strip, with an accessible lightbox. Copied to your site in the background. Screenshots are the publisher’s images: show them for your own games or where you have the right to.
  • Steam® News: your latest Steam announcements or patch notes, with title, date, and a short excerpt.

Place a gallery or news block next to a widget, and it picks up the widget’s game automatically. Or insert the “Game showcase” pattern: a widget with its screenshot gallery below.

Made to convert

  • A “Play the free demo” button for games with a demo. By default, a demo’s own widget asks visitors to “Wishlist the full game”, and a soundtrack’s offers “Get the soundtrack on Steam”. Demos, DLCs, and soundtracks get a badge and a link to the full game.
  • The Steam price for the widget’s store region, refreshed hourly by default, including sale discounts that disappear when the sale ends.
  • Optional Steam review summary (“Very Positive · 87% of 899,149 reviews”), Metacritic score, and genres.
  • Age ratings: the USK rating (Germany’s rating board) as the publisher entered it on Steam, otherwise the game’s Steam age gate.
  • Your own button text, and a heading level (H2 to H4) that fits your page outline.

Measure every placement

  • Impression, wishlist-click, and demo-click events for Google Analytics (GA4) via Google Tag Manager, Matomo Tag Manager, or classic Matomo. You can rename the events.
  • UTM parameters on every store link of the widget, plus a placement key per widget. The same key is the placement of your analytics events and the utm_content in Steam’s UTM report, so both reports name the same widget.
  • A tsi:track JavaScript event for any other analytics stack.

Privacy-friendly by design

  • Game data, header images, and screenshots are fetched by your server and stored on your site. Your visitors’ browsers normally contact Valve only when they click a link to Steam; the two exceptions are listed under External services.
  • The plugin sets no cookies. Its analytics events go through your existing tag manager or Matomo setup, so your consent rules still apply.
  • A privacy policy suggestion is included (Settings → Privacy → Policy Guide), and every external service is listed below.

Fast and low-maintenance

  • Steam data is cached and refreshed in the background, so page views normally do not wait for Steam.
  • Built-in SVG feature icons: no icon font to load.
  • Self-cleaning image cache with a size limit.

For publishers and agencies

  • Game Presets: save App ID, language, and UTM values once. Link widgets to a preset and they follow later changes. Export and import presets as JSON.
  • [steam_widget] shortcode for the game widget in the Classic Editor, page builders, and widget areas.
  • WP-CLI commands to warm and clear caches and to move presets between sites.
  • Fully translated into German, informal (“du”) and formal (“Sie”). The block settings appear in each user’s own WordPress language.

How it compares

  • Official Steam store widget: free and always current, but it’s an iframe that loads from Valve in your visitors’ browsers, has a fixed size and design, and sends no events to your analytics. To add UTM parameters, you edit its iframe URL.
  • This plugin: also free, rendered on your server, responsive, measurable per placement, and extended with a screenshot gallery and news.

This plugin is not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Valve Corporation. Steam and the Steam logo are trademarks or registered trademarks of Valve Corporation in the U.S. and/or other countries.

External services

The plugin shows data from Steam, a service of Valve Corporation. Your WordPress server makes all requests to Steam server-side. Apart from the two exceptions under “Steam image CDN” below, your visitors’ browsers make no requests to Valve. Nothing about your visitors is sent. Every request carries your server’s IP address and WordPress’s user agent (the WordPress version and your site’s URL), like any request WordPress makes.

  • Steam Subscriber Agreement
  • Valve Privacy Policy

Steam Store API (store.steampowered.com)

  • https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails: game data (name, description, price, release date, platforms, features, genres, age rating, Metacritic score, header image URL). What is sent: the App ID, the Steam language, and the country code of the price region. When: when a page with one of the plugin’s blocks is rendered (also in the editor preview) and no cached response exists, or in the background (WP-Cron) once the cached one is older than its cache time; when someone picks a game in the editor’s “Find a game by name”; in the gallery’s background copy job; in the hourly background refresh of your Game Presets and recently shown games; when you save or import Game Presets or click “Load Game Presets now”; with “Test connection” in debug mode; and when you run wp tsi cache warm. Responses are cached for one hour (adjustable up to 24 hours on the Cache tab), failed requests for 2 minutes. If Steam asks the plugin to wait, it waits that long: at least 2 minutes and at most 6 hours.
  • https://store.steampowered.com/api/storesearch/: the editor’s “Find a game by name”. What is sent: the search text (at least 3 characters), the Steam language, and the country code. When: a user who can edit posts searches in the block editor. Results are cached for 1 hour; at most 30 searches per minute reach Steam per site. The search text is not logged.
  • https://store.steampowered.com/api/dlcforapp/: a game’s DLC list. Not requested by any feature in this version; the plugin’s Steam client supports it, and the changelog will name the feature that starts to use it. What would be sent: the App ID, the Steam language, and the country code.

Steam Web API (api.steampowered.com)

Each method is used only by the feature named here. Valve serves GetItems and GetAppReviews without a key but does not list them as public, so they may change; GetNewsForApp is a documented public method. If a response changes, the feature shows nothing instead of breaking the page.

  • https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1/: the review summary, the end date of a sale, and which screenshots Steam marks as mature. What is sent: App IDs, the Steam language, and the country code. When: when a page is rendered (also in the editor preview) with a widget that has “Show Review Summary” on or shows a game on sale, or with a Screenshot Gallery, and no cached response exists; and in the gallery’s background copy job. Cached for 6 hours (review summary) or 1 hour (15 minutes while a discount runs); the list of mature screenshots for 7 days.
  • https://api.steampowered.com/IUserReviewsService/GetAppReviews/v1/: the review summary when GetItems has none (only for widgets with “Show Review Summary” on). What is sent: the App ID, the Steam language, and the review language filter. Cached for 6 hours. Steam also returns one individual user review; the plugin discards it and never stores it.
  • https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamNews/GetNewsForApp/v2/: the developers’ announcements for the Steam News block. What is sent: the App ID (for a demo, DLC, or soundtrack, that of its full game), the number of posts (10), the text length (0, the full text, which your server shortens to an excerpt), the news feed (developer announcements only; press feeds are never requested), and with “Patch notes only” the tag patchnotes. When: when a page with a Steam News block is rendered (also in the editor preview) and no cached response exists. Cached for 1 hour: title, URL, date, and a plain-text excerpt per post; the author’s Steam name only if the block opts in.

Steam image CDN (*.steamstatic.com, *.akamaihd.net)

Header images are downloaded from the URLs Steam provides when a widget for the game is first rendered or warmed (Game Presets, the hourly refresh, wp tsi cache warm), (not by a preview in the block editor of a user who cannot upload files: that shows a stored copy, or Steam’s URL in that user’s own editor), and again when the stored copy is missing or damaged, after clearing caches or “Refresh now”, or after the daily cleanup removed it (older than 30 days, or to keep the image cache under 50 MB). Gallery screenshots are downloaded only by a background job (WP-Cron), never while a page is shown, and only for galleries on published content or previewed by users who may upload files; the daily cleanup deletes a game’s copies once no gallery has shown them for 30 days. Both are stored in wp-content/uploads/terovania-game-marketing-widgets-for-steam/, and your visitors load them from your site. What is sent: the image request (its URL contains the App ID).

Two exceptions, in which your visitors’ browsers load images from Valve’s CDN and send it their IP address, browser data, and usually your page’s URL:

  • If a header image cannot be stored (for example, because the uploads folder is not writable), the widget shows it from Steam’s URL until a local copy exists. The plugin tries again after 30 minutes.
  • A gallery whose “Load screenshots from” setting is “Steam’s CDN” (opt-in) shows its screenshots from Steam’s URLs. This usually requires your visitors’ consent; the filter tsi_gallery_steam_cdn can withhold it until your consent tool reports consent.

Links

The widget’s buttons and links lead to store.steampowered.com with your UTM parameters; news titles lead to the post on Steam. A visitor’s browser contacts Steam only when the visitor clicks. With “Show Metacritic Score” on, the score links to metacritic.com; the plugin loads nothing from Metacritic.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins → Add New Plugin, search for “Game Marketing Widgets for Steam”, then install and activate it.
  2. Open Steam Widgets in the admin menu and set your defaults: game, language, UTM source and campaign, and your analytics integration.
  3. In the block editor, add the Steam® Game Widget block, type your game’s name under Find a game by name, and pick it.
  4. Optional: add the Steam® Screenshot Gallery or Steam® News block next to the widget. Or start with the Game showcase pattern (a widget with its gallery) instead of step 3.
  5. Optional: in Google Tag Manager or Matomo Tag Manager, create triggers for the widget’s events (see the FAQ). Classic Matomo needs no setup.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Steam API key or Steamworks access?

No. The plugin uses Steam’s public store data and needs no key and no Steamworks login. You only need your game’s App ID, or its name: the editor finds it for you.

Is it GDPR-friendly? Does it set cookies?

The plugin sets no cookies, and your visitors’ browsers normally load nothing from Valve: your server fetches the data and images and serves them from your site. There are two exceptions, explained under External services: a header image that cannot be stored on your site is shown from Steam’s URL, and a Screenshot Gallery you set to load from Steam’s CDN (opt-in). Whether your site complies with the GDPR depends on your whole setup: your analytics tool (GA4, Matomo) still needs your consent setup, and a text for your privacy policy is included under Settings → Privacy → Policy Guide.

Will it slow down my site?

Steam data is cached (1 hour by default) and refreshed in the background, so after a game’s first view, page views normally do not wait for Steam. Images are served from your site, the feature icons are inline SVG, and the small frontend script has no dependencies. Game Presets and wp tsi cache warm load a game before its first visitor.

How do I track wishlist clicks in GA4 or Matomo?

Choose your integration under Steam Widgets → General → Analytics Integration. The widget then sends steamWidgetImpression, steamWishlistClick, and steamDemoClick with appId, gameName, and placement; click events also carry ctaType and utmContent.

In Google Tag Manager, create Data Layer Variables for these fields, a Custom Event trigger per event, and a GA4 event tag; then register the fields as custom dimensions in GA4. Divide clicks by impressions per placement to get each placement’s click-through rate. Matomo Tag Manager receives the same events in its _mtm data layer; classic Matomo tracks them as events in the category “Steam Widget”.

Without Google Tag Manager (gtag.js only), forward the events yourself: document.addEventListener( 'tsi:track', function ( e ) { gtag( 'event', e.detail.event, e.detail ); } );

How do I connect my analytics to Steam’s UTM report?

Give a widget its own UTM Content (placement), for example homepage-hero, or keep the automatic key (widget-p42-1 for the first widget in post 42). The key is the placement of the widget’s events and the utm_content of its Steam links. In Steamworks, open UTM Analytics for the app the link leads to and compare its wishlists per utm_content with your clicks per placement. The demo button adds -demo to the key and lands in the demo’s report. The automatic key follows the widget’s position in the post, so adding or moving widgets above it changes the key: give placements you compare over time their own short, lower-case key.

Can I show demos, DLCs, soundtracks, or unreleased games?

Yes. Enter the App ID or pick it in the search. Demos, DLCs, and soundtracks get a badge and a link to the full game, and a demo’s default button wishlists the full game. Unreleased games show “Coming soon”, which makes the widget a good fit for pre-launch pages.

Which price and language does the widget show?

The price of the widget’s language region (US dollars for English, euros for German, and so on), including Steam sales. Steam texts come in the language you pick per widget (27 Steam languages); when Steam has no text in that language, the widget shows Steam’s English store data, including the US price. If rules for advertising price reductions apply to your site, switch off Sale prices under Steam Widgets → General (or “Show Sale Prices” for one widget) to show only the current price.

Can I change the look?

Pick one of three layouts, the title’s heading level, your own button text, and which details appear: price, sale prices, age rating, feature icons, genres, review summary, Metacritic score, release status, badges, and the demo button. The shortcode also accepts hex colors for the button and the release status (cta_color, cta_hover_color, highlight_color).

Does it work with the Classic Editor and page builders?

Yes, for the game widget: use the [steam_widget] shortcode. It renders the same markup as the block, and every block setting has an attribute, for example:

[steam_widget appid="913800" layout="compact" utm_content="sidebar" show_reviews="true"]

[steam_widget preset="Spring Sale"] links the widget to a Game Preset. The Screenshot Gallery and Steam News are available as blocks only.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes. Settings, presets, caches and the debug log belong to each site. After network activation, every site sets itself up on its first visit, and sites created later are set up right away. Network deactivation removes the plugin’s scheduled tasks from every site, and deleting the plugin removes its data from every site. On a very large network, delete it with wp plugin uninstall rather than in the browser, which may time out.

Can I manage it with WP-CLI?

Yes:

  • wp tsi cache clear clears all cached Steam data; wp tsi cache clear 620 refreshes one game.
  • wp tsi cache warm 620 --language=en or --all-presets loads games before the first visitor does.
  • wp tsi cache stats shows the cache size.
  • wp tsi presets export and wp tsi presets import presets.json move presets between sites.
  • wp tsi diagnostics shows the Steam request log recorded in debug mode.

Can developers change what the plugin does?

Yes, with filters in a theme or a small plugin. Each one is documented in the plugin’s code where it is applied. Example: add_filter( 'tsi_feature_icons_max', function () { return 5; } );

  • Display: tsi_feature_icons (the feature chips, keyed by Steam category ID: add, relabel, reorder, or switch off entries), tsi_feature_icons_max (default 8; 0 hides the chips), tsi_icon_sprite_inline, tsi_gallery_legal_notice.
  • Tracking: tsi_tracking_event_names, tsi_widget_instance_id.
  • Steam requests and cache: tsi_steam_endpoints, tsi_steam_api_timeout, tsi_cache_ttl, tsi_cache_ttl_failure, tsi_steam_stale_ttl, tsi_discount_end_check, tsi_search_rate_limit, tsi_refresh_cache_batch, tsi_preset_warm_max, tsi_preset_warm_budget.
  • Images and gallery: tsi_image_allowed_hosts, tsi_image_cache_max_bytes, tsi_image_cache_max_age, tsi_image_failure_ttl, tsi_screenshot_batch_size, tsi_gallery_steam_cdn, tsi_gallery_mature_min_age, tsi_gallery_mature_descriptor_ids, tsi_legacy_cleanup_batch_size, tsi_legacy_cleanup_step_seconds.
  • Settings page: tsi_settings_tabs adds a tab; the action tsi_settings_tab_{slug} prints its content.
  • Multisite: tsi_network_batch_size (sites per batch when network deactivation or deleting the plugin cleans every site, default 100).

The widget says “Game data could not be loaded”. What now?

Open Steam Widgets → Diagnostics and switch on Debug mode. The tab lists the last 20 Steam requests with their status, and Test connection asks Steam for your default game right away. Switch debug mode off again when you are done.
sections.changelog:
1.2.1

The first release on WordPress.org since 1.0.5: includes everything listed under 1.2.0, 1.1.0, and 1.0.6.

  • Fixed: the Screenshot Gallery shows the publisher’s legal notice only under its screenshots, no longer under the placeholder while the screenshots are still being copied.
  • Fixed: in the lightbox, screen readers hear a screenshot’s caption once instead of twice.
  • Fixed: the lightbox buttons’ icons sit centered on every device, and on phones the arrows are directly below the screenshot instead of at the bottom of the screen.
  • Changed: the publisher’s legal notice under the gallery is collapsed under one short line, and the new block option “Show the publisher’s legal notice” turns it off (for your own game, when your site already shows the notice).

1.2.0

Includes everything from 1.0.6 and 1.1.0, which were not released on WordPress.org. Most important for 1.0.5 users: the fix for the header image copies that filled the uploads folder (see 1.0.6), and the changes marked “Changed” below.

  • New: Steam® Screenshot Gallery block with an accessible lightbox. Screenshots are copied to your site in the background.
  • New: Steam® News block for your latest announcements or patch notes.
  • New: optional Steam review summary and Metacritic score.
  • New: Find a game by name in the block editor.
  • New: linked presets that follow later changes (a value set in the block itself wins over the preset), plus preset export and import.
  • New: a placement key per widget, used as utm_content and as the placement of analytics events.
  • Changed: Steam links now use the widget’s placement key as utm_content instead of the fixed value gutenberg-widget, so clicks after the update appear under new values in Steam’s UTM report. To keep a widget’s old row, set its UTM Content (placement) to gutenberg-widget.
  • New: rename the tracking events in the settings.
  • New: WP-CLI commands for caches and presets.
  • New: a privacy policy suggestion under Settings → Privacy → Policy Guide.
  • New: a formal German translation (“Sie”) for sites set to “Deutsch (Sie)”; they used to see the plugin in English.
  • Improved: built-in SVG feature icons replace the Dashicons font (about 60 KB less for your visitors). To keep the old icons, choose “Dashicons” under Steam Widgets → General → Feature icons.
  • Improved: once a game is cached, page views normally no longer wait for Steam: expired data is shown while it refreshes in the background. The cache time is adjustable up to 24 hours.
  • Improved: sale prices disappear on time when a sale ends and can be turned off per widget.
  • Improved: the settings page has tabs (General, Presets, Cache, Diagnostics) and “Refresh now” for a single game.
  • Changed: new names that match the plugin: the admin menu is Steam Widgets (was “Steam Integration”), the block is Steam® Game Widget (was “Steam® Integration Widget”). Existing blocks, shortcodes, and settings are unchanged.
  • Changed: the block settings no longer show the locked “Colors (Premium)” panel. Button and highlight colors stay available through the shortcode (cta_color, cta_hover_color, highlight_color). The optional credit line under the widget is one translatable sentence, and its link is marked nofollow.
  • Fixed: UTM values with spaces, “&”, or “#” reach Steam intact; square brackets in Steam texts no longer run as shortcodes; accessibility fixes on the settings page.
  • Fixed: screen readers now hear which game a widget shows, the language of Steam’s texts, and which links open a new tab; the button’s hover and focus color has enough contrast; the lightbox reacts to swipes anywhere on the screen; right-to-left sites and Windows high-contrast mode are supported.
  • Changed: the daily cleanup also deletes a game’s gallery copies once no gallery has shown them for 30 days (the existing filter tsi_image_cache_max_age sets the age for both), and when the image cache is over its size limit it first removes the images that were neither downloaded nor shown for the longest time. Galleries in a contributor’s preview are copied once the post is published.
  • Changed: the widget’s CSS variables are now --tsi-widget-bg, --tsi-text-color, --tsi-highlight-color, --tsi-cta-bg, --tsi-cta-bg-hover and --tsi-link-color, set on .wp-block-terovania-steam-widget instead of :root, so they no longer clash with a theme’s own variables. Custom CSS that set the old names on :root must use the new names on that class.
  • Note: 1.x is the last release series that supports PHP 7.4 and WordPress 6.0; 2.0 will raise both minimums.

1.1.0

  • New: badges and full-game links for demos, DLCs, and soundtracks, and a “Play the free demo” button.
  • Changed: during a Steam sale, the widget now shows the discount, the original price struck through, and the sale price (1.0.5 showed the current price only). If rules for advertising price reductions apply to your site (in the EU, for example, stating the lowest price of the last 30 days), switch off Sale prices under Steam Widgets → General.
  • Changed: a demo widget with the default button text now wishlists the full game; its click event reports the full game as appId and the demo as sourceAppId.
  • Changed: on sites in German, the widget’s labels and its default button text are German (“Auf die Steam-Wunschliste”); a button text you typed yourself is shown as typed.
  • New: genres, more feature icons, a heading level setting, and debug mode with a Steam request log; the block editor controls are translated.
  • Fixed: official USK ratings are shown correctly. Steam’s generated rating, which 1.0.5 showed, now appears only with “Show Steam-Generated Age Rating” and is never labeled as USK.
  • Fixed: a visible focus ring on every widget link, and screen readers read the release date and age badge as plain text.

1.0.6

  • Fixed: 1.0.5 stored a new copy of the header image on every page view. The update removes the copies automatically in the background; “Clean up now” on the Cache tab removes a large backlog at once.
  • Changed: new card design: the feature icons are labeled chips under the header image, and the button is always last (full width on phones).
  • Changed: Steam responses are cached (1 hour by default), so a new price, a sale start, or a release can take up to twice the cache time to appear; “Refresh now” on the Cache tab updates one game at once.
  • Changed: deleting the plugin removes all its data, including Game Presets (export them first).
  • New: [steam_widget] shortcode, Game Presets, Compact and Vertical layouts, Matomo support, and a German translation.
  • Fixed: tracking works with plugins that delay JavaScript.

1.0.5 and earlier

  • Toolbar controls for App ID and language, English fallback for Steam texts, local image caching, UTM parameters, and impression tracking.

When: a user who can edit posts searches in the block editor. Results are cached for 1 hour; at most 30 searches per minute reach Steam per site. The search text is not logged.
  • https://store.steampowered.com/api/dlcforapp/: a game’s DLC list. Not requested by any feature in this version; the plugin’s Steam client supports it, and the changelog will name the feature that starts to use it. What would be sent: the App ID, the Steam language, and the country code.

Steam Web API (api.steampowered.com)

Each method is used only by the feature named here. Valve serves GetItems and GetAppReviews without a key but does not list them as public, so they may change; GetNewsForApp is a documented public method. If a response changes, the feature shows nothing instead of breaking the page.

  • https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreBrowseService/GetItems/v1/: the review summary, the end date of a sale, and which screenshots Steam marks as mature. What is sent: App IDs, the Steam language, and the country code. When: when a page is rendered (also in the editor preview) with a widget that has “Show Review Summary” on or shows a game on sale, or with a Screenshot Gallery, and no cached response exists; and in the gallery’s background copy job. Cached for 6 hours (review summary) or 1 hour (15 minutes while a discount runs); the list of mature screenshots for 7 days.
  • https://api.steampowered.com/IUserReviewsService/GetAppReviews/v1/: the review summary when GetItems has none (only for widgets with “Show Review Summary” on). What is sent: the App ID, the Steam language, and the review language filter. Cached for 6 hours. Steam also returns one individual user review; the plugin discards it and never stores it.
  • https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamNews/GetNewsForApp/v2/: the developers’ announcements for the Steam News block. What is sent: the App ID (for a demo, DLC, or soundtrack, that of its full game), the number of posts (10), the text length (0, the full text, which your server shortens to an excerpt), the news feed (developer announcements only; press feeds are never requested), and with “Patch notes only” the tag patchnotes. When: when a page with a Steam News block is rendered (also in the editor preview) and no cached response exists. Cached for 1 hour: title, URL, date, and a plain-text excerpt per post; the author’s Steam name only if the block opts in.

Steam image CDN (*.steamstatic.com, *.akamaihd.net)

Header images are downloaded from the URLs Steam provides when a widget for the game is first rendered or warmed (Game Presets, the hourly refresh, wp tsi cache warm), (not by a preview in the block editor of a user who cannot upload files: that shows a stored copy, or Steam’s URL in that user’s own editor), and again when the stored copy is missing or damaged, after clearing caches or “Refresh now”, or after the daily cleanup removed it (older than 30 days, or to keep the image cache under 50 MB). Gallery screenshots are downloaded only by a background job (WP-Cron), never while a page is shown, and only for galleries on published content or previewed by users who may upload files; the daily cleanup deletes a game’s copies once no gallery has shown them for 30 days. Both are stored in wp-content/uploads/terovania-game-marketing-widgets-for-steam/, and your visitors load them from your site. What is sent: the image request (its URL contains the App ID).

Two exceptions, in which your visitors’ browsers load images from Valve’s CDN and send it their IP address, browser data, and usually your page’s URL:

  • If a header image cannot be stored (for example, because the uploads folder is not writable), the widget shows it from Steam’s URL until a local copy exists. The plugin tries again after 30 minutes.
  • A gallery whose “Load screenshots from” setting is “Steam’s CDN” (opt-in) shows its screenshots from Steam’s URLs. This usually requires your visitors’ consent; the filter tsi_gallery_steam_cdn can withhold it until your consent tool reports consent.

Links

The widget’s buttons and links lead to store.steampowered.com with your UTM parameters; news titles lead to the post on Steam. A visitor’s browser contacts Steam only when the visitor clicks. With “Show Metacritic Score” on, the score links to metacritic.com; the plugin loads nothing from Metacritic.

The block editor: find your game by name, link the widget to a preset, and see a live preview.
